answer: Requiring a non-transferable, slashed stake per identity stops Sybil swarms because each account must lock real capital before it can take part. An attacker wanting a thousand agents needs a thousand bonds, so marginal cost grows linearly with swarm size. A watchdog can act as a falcon that flags clusters of thin, newly bonded accounts, and correlated stake is the signal of a coordinated puppet ring. Like a vine that must root before it climbs, identity here must be anchored in money before it acts.
